learning_outcomes.text: Students will have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, although supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students will know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences usually demonstrated by developing and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.

Students will have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Students will be able to transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Students will have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Choose and apply the most appropriate methods and techniques to analyze and solve problems defined by data that represent a challenge due to their volume, velocity, variety, or heterogeneity, including computational, mathematical, statistical, and signal processing methods.

Possess experimental and analytical skills to work autonomously, being able to design experiments and to describe, analyze, evaluate, and interpret the resulting information to propose alternative and novel solutions to known and/or emerging problems.
Create models and make decisions based on available data, combining acquired knowledge and being able to apply new knowledge for problem-solving.
Ability to integrate into a multidisciplinary team within the framework of a data science project.
Ability to express the results of data processing clearly and convincingly, both in writing and orally.
Analyze data from complex phenomena by applying statistical techniques and probability calculus.
Understand and correctly apply exploratory data analysis and statistical modeling techniques, evaluating the quality of the models, validating them, and interpreting them.
Know and apply the main techniques of Descriptive Statistics, determining the most appropriate for each data set based on its characteristics.
Know the main data collection techniques and the most common errors in a sampling process.
Apply punctual estimation techniques for unknown parameters from a sample, and determine the error associated with the estimation.
Construct confidence intervals for the main parameters of interest in the context of data analysis, and determine the minimum sample size to bound the error committed with a given confidence level.
Fluently handle the concepts of statistic, critical region, significance level, and p-value.
Be able to test hypotheses about proportions and means, both with independent and paired samples, determining the ideal type of test for each situation.

syllabus_topics: Statistical summary of data: frequency tables, graphical representations, summary measures.
Data collection techniques. Introduction to statistical inference.
Confidence intervals. Confidence level and error bounds. Sample sizes.
Introduction to hypothesis testing. Significance level, critical region, and p-value.

Examples of hypothesis tests. Proportions: comparison of one or several proportions. Normal populations: comparison of one or several populations. Paired samples and independent samples. ANOVA and ANCOVA.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance, participation in seminars and tutorials, including online (PA)
Active participation in forums and/or Campus Virtual activities (AC)
Reports, lab reports, and/or practical exams (PL)

assessment_rules: The final grade in the ordinary and extraordinary calls is calculated as 0.05 x PA + 0.15 x AC + 0.2 x PL + 0.6 x EX. For differentiated evaluation, the procedure is an 80% theoretical-practical exam and a 20% laboratory test. In all cases, the final grade must be at least 5 out of 10 to pass the course. Students presenting for any extraordinary call assessment implicitly waive the corresponding ordinary call grade.
